title: Build an app with just your phone (cloud)

steps.title: What we'll do today
steps.html:
You'll build an app with just your phone, no computer. Tell Claude on your phone, it builds the app in the cloud, and you install that app on your phone's home screen.

Tell it on your phonebuilt in the cloudPR → mergeturn on PagesYour app's addressAdd to Home ScreenPhone app
  • Time: 25 minutes
  • You need: experience with Phone 2 (GitHub sign-up, Claude connected) and Phone 3 (cloud jobs), and a paid Claude plan
  • The app: the same workout timer as App 1 (finished example ↗)

If GitHub words (repository, PR, merge) are new, see GitHub at a glance first.

steps.title: Make a public repository for the app
steps.html:
1. In your phone browser (or the GitHub app): github.com → + → New repository.
  2. Name: my-timer · Public · tick Add a README file → Create repository.
This time it's Public. A free app address (GitHub Pages) needs a public repository, so anyone can read the files. Never put names, phone numbers, passwords or API keys in it. Leave your notes repository my-notes private.

check.q: Was my-timer created, with a Public label?

steps.title: If making the repository doesn't work
steps.html:
• No + on your phone? Menu (☰) at the top left → Repositories → New.
  • No GitHub account? Start with the sign-up step in Phone 2.

steps.title: Let Claude into my-timer
steps.html:
In Phone 2 you installed the Claude app on my-notes only. Add the new repository to the list.

  1. GitHub → profile at the top right → Settings → Applications → Configure next to Claude.
  2. Keep Only select repositories, add my-timer → Save.

Tapping Configure at github.com/apps/claude gets you to the same screen.

check.q: In the Claude phone app → Code, is my-timer in the repository list?

steps.title: If my-timer isn't listed
steps.html:
• Check you added my-timer on the Configure screen and tapped Save.
  • Pull down to refresh the list, or open claude.ai/code in your phone browser.
  • Never connected Claude before? Do Phone 2 first.

steps.title: Describe it on your phone and have it built
steps.html:
1. Claude phone app → Code.
  2. Pick the repository my-timer (branch main) and send the sentence below.
  3. It takes a few minutes. It keeps working even if you close the app.

There are no permission cards in the cloud. Instead the result lands on a new branch, and only your merge makes it count. (Phone 3)
steps.alt: Picking my-timer in Code on the phone and describing the app
steps.code: Build a workout timer web app as index.html. A big start button, a 20-second ring timer, read out 'three, two, one' in English for the last 3 seconds, fitted to a phone screen. Also make a manifest named 'Workout timer' and a stopwatch icon on a blue background (PNG) so it opens like an app from the home screen

check.q: Do you see that it pushed to a new branch, and a Changes count?

steps.title: If it's slow or seems stuck
steps.html:
• The first run takes longer while the cloud computer gets ready. Give it about 5 minutes.
  • Claude may have asked you something. Open the chat and answer.
  • If it's paused for a while, send "carry on".

steps.title: Create a PR and merge it
steps.html:
1. Tap Create PR. No button? Send "Create a PR".
  2. In your phone browser: github.com → my-timer → Pull requests → the new PR.
  3. Check Files changed has index.html, the manifest and icons → Merge pull request → Confirm merge.

You don't have to read all the code. Just check which files are added, and that nothing odd (like passwords) is there.
steps.alt: After finishing, Changes and a Create PR button appear

check.q: Can you see index.html on my-timer's front page (Code)?

steps.title: If merging doesn't work
steps.html:
• Creating and merging a PR is the same as in Phone 3.
  • If index.html ended up inside a folder, say "Move index.html to the top (root) of the repository". Pages opens the index.html at the top.

steps.title: Turn on GitHub Pages and get the app's address
steps.html:
1. my-timer repository → Settings. (On a phone, swipe the menu along the top of the repository or look under ⋯)
  2. Pages in the side (or bottom) menu.
  3. Source: Deploy from a branch · Branch: main · / (root) → Save.
  4. After 1–2 minutes, refresh: Your site is live at https://your-id.github.io/my-timer/ appears. Tap it and check the timer opens.
steps.alt: Choosing main and Save in Settings → Pages in a phone browser, with the address shown

check.q: Does the timer open at https://your-id.github.io/my-timer/?

steps.title: If Settings is hidden, or you get a 404
steps.html:
• The narrow phone screen can hide menus. Turn on Desktop site in your browser menu to see the computer layout.
  • 404: the first time takes a few minutes. Also check index.html is at the top of the repository.
  • If Pages shows an upgrade notice, the repository is Private. Settings → bottom Change visibility → Public.

steps.title: Install it on your home screen
steps.html:
Install it straight from the app address you just opened.

  • Android (Chrome): ⋮ at the top right → Add to Home screen (or Install app).
  • iPhone (Safari): Share (□↑) at the bottom → Add to Home Screen.

Tap the Workout timer icon on your home screen. Your own app, built on your phone and installed on your phone.
steps.alt: A Workout timer icon on the phone's home screen

check.q: Does it open from the home screen icon, and does the timer work?

steps.title: If Add to Home Screen is missing or odd
steps.html:
• On iPhone, only Safari can add to the home screen.
  • If the icon shows a letter, ask Claude "Add an iPhone home screen icon (apple-touch-icon) too" → PR → merge.
  • No sound? Check the phone isn't on silent.

steps.title: Update it from your phone too
steps.html:
1. Open the same chat in the Claude app's Code list and send what to change.
  2. Merge the new (or same) PR, and the app updates 1–2 minutes later. Close and reopen the home screen app.
  • Merging is your final permission: check Files changed before tapping.
  • Public repository: no personal data, passwords or API keys.
  • Usage: the cloud uses the same limits as chat and desktop.
steps.code: Change it to 20 seconds of work and 10 seconds of rest, repeated 3 times. Make the timer green during rest

steps.title: 🎉 App practice 3 done! An app built on your phone
steps.html:
With just your phone, no computer, you built an app, published it and installed it. Now one sentence on your commute — "add this feature" — can grow your app.

App 1–2Build on a computer → upload yourself → Pages
App 3Tell it on your phone → built in the cloud → merge the PR → Pages

Three things to remember

  1. The app repository is public for Pages. Keep sensitive data out.
  2. In the cloud, PR → merge replaces permission cards. Check Files changed before merging.
  3. To update: say it in the same chat → merge.

Earlln's EarllnCore was built on a phone just like this. The next lesson turns it into an Android app (APK).
